assessments.reasoning: The TRY usage section describes stopping execution of the TRY body when it throws and considering typed catch handlers in textual order. A compatible handler accepts the declared type or an exception descended from it.

challenge.method: Compare an exact-type match, a descendant-type match, an incompatible first handler followed by a compatible handler, and the absence of any match. Consult the separate FINALLY return restriction.
challenge.results: For thrown exceptions in a valid TRY body, a compatible earlier handler determines the stated branch; an incompatible handler does not. The no-match example continues into the documented unwinding control. The FINALLY return warning concerns that separate scope and supplies no exception to the cited matching sequence.

limitations: No handler-thrown exception, FINALLY control transfer, or runtime diagnostic behavior is qualified.
